name: WCORR-WEB-004: PHP file creation followed by HTTP access attempt
description: This is the revised version. Instead of accepting general suspicious web activity after PHP creation, it requires a subsequent HTTP request targeting a PHP URL within the WordPress uploads directory.
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=30m
  [any where rule.id.keyword == "554"
    and syscheck.event.keyword == "added"
    and syscheck.path.keyword like
      "/var/lib/docker/volumes/web_wp_data/_data/wp-content/uploads/*.php"]
  [any where data.url.keyword != null
    and data.url.keyword like
      "/wp-content/uploads/*.php*"]
author: Wazuh EQL Correlation
false_positives: The requested PHP URL is not verified against the exact created file. Nested upload paths are included; the request stage deliberately has no rule-ID restriction, allowing other classifications including 31101.
setup: Collect added-file FIM at the exact WordPress Docker volume path and native URL telemetry for uploads requests.
